terra.problem: Calling it the call that never came treats Ephraim's complaint as fact. Jephthah says he did call them.
Jephthah says Ephraim did not save him, not that they did not answer his call.
The big-talk punchline makes light of Ephraim's defeat in a deadly conflict and laughs at the defeated group.
The instruction to mind your words is preachy and directs a scolding at the baker.
Jephthah standing right there when the Ephraimites made the remark is not established by the text.
The verse describes what happened when a fugitive from Ephraim asked to cross. It does not say everyone who wanted to cross had to answer.
The Amalekites do not appear as people in the passage. Their name identifies the hill country where Abdon was buried.
“Wrong place” uses a prohibited word to characterize the baker's answer.
“You're thinking of” assumes why the baker chose the answer, which Papa Dorin cannot know.
Jephthah's and Abdon's burials do not come one right after the other. Ibzan's and Elon's burials are between them.
Calling Gilead Jephthah's home region adds a fact not established in this passage without a reference.
